name: Cowpea
form: Seed flour (whole or dehulled; see each value)
description: Widely grown Nigerian legume (beans). Good lysine source, low in fat.
processing: Typical route: sorting, soaking, dehulling, drying, milling. Dehulling reduces fibre and tannins; heat treatment reduces trypsin inhibitors. Values depend on variety and processing.

name: Bambara Groundnut
form: Seed flour (whole or dehulled; see each value)
description: Drought-tolerant underutilised legume, eaten as okpa in Nigeria. Hard-to-cook seed.
processing: Typical route: soaking, dehulling, drying, milling; often roasted or boiled. Long soaking or germination improves digestibility.

name: Defatted Groundnut
description: Groundnut flour or cake after oil removal (e.g. kuli-kuli cake, solvent-defatted flour). Treated as a separate ingredient from whole groundnut: defatting raises protein, lowers fat and changes functional properties, so whole-groundnut values must not be entered here.
processing: Oil removed by pressing (partial defatting, higher residual fat) or solvent extraction (lower residual fat), then milled. Residual fat, heat history and protein functionality depend on the extraction route; record it with every value. Must be screened for aflatoxin.

name: African Yam Bean
form: Seed flour (whole or dehulled; see each value)
description: Underutilised legume grown in southern Nigeria. Hard-to-cook seed with good amino acid balance.
processing: Typical route: soaking, boiling or dehulling, drying, milling. Processing strongly affects antinutrients and functional properties.

name: Soybean
description: High-protein oilseed legume widely processed in Nigeria (soy milk, soy-ogi, flour).
processing: Typical route: cleaning, dehulling, heat treatment (boiling or roasting) to inactivate trypsin inhibitors and lipoxygenase, drying, milling.
